instructions: Answer the questions below. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Section 3. You will hear a conversation between two students about a report on tribal culture in Borneo.

transcript.speaker: Gordon
transcript.text: Let's get started then, shall we Alice? So the piece about contemporary Borneo's tribes was really interesting – the one about current lifestyles of the tribal people.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: The article on the diversity of culture in tribal communities? Yeah, anthropologists were discovering shifts in food, hunting, harvesting; even music, dance and community structures are changing. It's quite unusual, isn't it Gordon?

transcript.speaker: Gordon
transcript.text: Yes, the article definitely has material we can include in our report. At first I was confused about which tribes were being studied – as the island of Borneo is the territory of Malaysia...

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: ...and Indonesia. Yes, but it seems they studied tribes from all over the island.

transcript.speaker: Gordon
transcript.text: That's right. But as I understand it, the article focuses mostly on how tribal traditions are going through changes because of modern pop culture.
transcript.highlight_text: changes because of modern pop culture.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Didn't the article say that was because of television?

transcript.speaker: Gordon
transcript.text: I think it was all media. Tribes in Indonesia, for example, would mostly get TV channels, radio stations, publications, and even web content from there. And many tribes had access to media from both countries and so they were being persuaded by both to alter their traditional way of living.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Oh, yes. The author uses the concept ‘media influence’ to describe this phenomenon.
transcript.highlight_text: The author uses the concept ‘media influence’

transcript.speaker: Gordon
transcript.text: Using this concept, I thought we could do a comparison study. Find research data on tribal culture from the past, and compare it to more current data.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: OK, that sounds like a good approach. How should we start?

transcript.speaker: Gordon
transcript.text: So, we'd need to first see how much other information is out there... other articles or reports... or we could just track down actual tribal members currently living in Borneo. You know... use social media sites to collect current data.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Or, do a bit of both. Not everyone will be able to access social media sites. So, it would be good to include statistics from other studies that included a broader selection of tribal members.
transcript.highlight_text: good to include statistics from other studies

transcript.speaker: Gordon
transcript.text: That's right. Then we might still need to gather older data regarding past traditions so that we can do the comparison. I did read another article about the tribal people in...
